newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gold Fields' Q4 gains clouded by weak gold.
newsitem.headline: Gold Fields' Q4 gains clouded by weak gold.

text.p: Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd on Thursday posted satisfactory fourth quarter gold profits after a grim third quarter, but warned that the weaker bullion price would still take its toll.

"It has been a satisfactory quarter in that what was anticipated has been achieved -- that is an improvement in all the divisions, with the exception of the Kloof division," chief executive of gold operations Alan Munro said.
"I think the magnitude of the achievement might come as a surprise to some of you," he added.

When third quarter results were announced in October, analysts termed them "wretched" and wondered whether Gold Fields, the world's second largest gold producer, would be able to pull itself back from the edge of the abyss.
Gold Fields on Thursday announced pre-capex earnings for the three months to end-December of 333.08 million rand -- a 21 percent improvement on the September quarter's 274.41 million rand.
Munro cautioned that the December quarter's figures excluded the impact of the Christmas holidays, which were likely to affect the current three months to end-March.
Furthermore, he said that bullion's recent slide pointed to an obviously weaker period for the metal price, which would no doubt affect Gold Fields' earnings.
But he added that the mining house would attempt to counter this negative impact by maximising production.

"That there is a danger of a weaker period ahead of us, I have no doubt. The most important thing that we can do is make our operations as efficient as possible," he said, adding that it was unclear what the bullion price was likely to do now.
Munro said that the longer-term effect of a weaker bullion price would concern Gold Fields as it would then need to review its long-term projects already under way.
Gold Fields raised its gold output in the fourth quarter to 22,902 kg from 21,172 kg previously.
Asked about Gold Fields' anti-hedging policy, Munro said:

"It is true that we do not have a forward position. Hindsight suggests that it might have been a good thing to have locked in a better price. We will work hard to ensure that without forward sales we still make a profit.
"We benefit from not making forward sales when the price is increasing and it is going to do that one of these days."
Looking further ahead, Munro said that the three months to end-June were likely to be difficult as they contained more public holidays.

The Kloof division was the single disappointing performer of the Gold Fields' stable. Output there declined to 5,513 kg from 5,753 kg, although overall production for the Kloof Gold Mining Co Ltd rose to 9,846.7 kg from 9,228.6 kg.
"The disappointment was we did not get the improvement in output that we anticipated (in the Kloof division)," Munro said.
He added that gold production in the Kloof division was not expected to improve in the March quarter.

Following violence last year at its gold mines which left scores of miners dead and halted production, Munro said that industrial relations on the mines were improving and would continue to move in a positive direction.
